name: NovaBox
rootCause: Constructor Dividend Checkpoint Bypass. Lost: 56.73 ETH

descriptions.text: Constructor Dividend Checkpoint Bypass. Lost: 56.73 ETH

NovaBox attempts to block contract depositors with an extcodesize(msg.sender) == 0 check, but a contract executing inside its own constructor has zero runtime code, so the check passes. Worse, when a new dual ETH/NOVA depositor is added to the dividend list, NovaBox does not initialize that depositor's dividend checkpoint to the current accumulator value. The attacker, using an Aave WETH flash loan and a NOVA seed, deposits NOVA and ETH from inside a constructor (bypassing the extcodesize gate), joins the dividend list with a zero checkpoint, then immediately withdraws its ETH and is paid out the entire historical ETH dividend accrued since the checkpoint origin - dividends it never earned. This nets ~56.73 ETH. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x0cfa357e9e4db1540246f17cb6bfa0634ff8727d7cf241b63fb22605021c8844 Analysis: https://x.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2064616360466919793

The NovaBox platform’s reward pool on Ethereum was hacked. The attacker borrowed 427.5 WETH via an Aave V3 flash loan and exploited a flaw in the reward distribution mechanism (dividends distributed before balance updates on deposits/withdrawals). By first depositing a small amount of NOVA tokens to trigger dividend calculation and then a large ETH deposit to inflate their actual share—while the system still calculated based on the old small share—they generated approximately 145.82 ETH in “phantom dividends,” draining the pool from 65.11 ETH to 0.09 ETH (99.86% loss) in a single transaction. Security firm F12 confirmed it was not a smart contract vuln…

NovaBox on Ethereum Mainnet suffered a $107,000 loss on 9 June 2026, when an attacker exploited a flaw in the reward distribution logic using a flash loan and a constructor-based deposit. The improperly sequenced dividend snapshot allowed the attacker to withdraw inflated dividends, nearly emptying the pool. The NovaBox contract took a dividend snapshot before updating the new depositor's balance, allowing attackers to collect unearned dividends by joining through a constructor contract and immediately withdrawing ETH. The flawed sequence enabled 'phantom' dividend allocations.
